entities.summary:
Enrique de Cardona y Enríquez (1485–1530) was a Spanish Roman Catholic cardinal and bishop. Born in Valencia, Spain, he rose to prominence within the Catholic Church, eventually becoming a cardinal in 1503. As a key figure in the Spanish Inquisition, he played a crucial role in the persecution of Jews, Muslims, and Protestants during the late 15th and early 16th centuries. His influence extended to the Catholic monarchs, Ferdinand and Isabella, who relied on him for spiritual guidance and counsel.

As the Inquisition's chief advisor, de Cardona y Enríquez oversaw the expulsion of Jews from Spain in 1492, a decree that would have far-reaching consequences for the country's economy, culture, and politics. He also participated in the persecution of Muslims, who were subjected to forced conversions, imprisonment, and execution.

De Cardona y Enríquez's legacy is complex and multifaceted. While he played a significant role in shaping the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation, his actions also contributed to the suffering of countless individuals and communities.

In the centuries that followed, de Cardona y Enríquez's name would become synonymous with the horrors of the Spanish Inquisition, a dark chapter in the country's history that would haunt its people for centuries to come.

The impact of de Cardona y Enríquez's actions can still be felt today, as the legacy of the Inquisition continues to influence contemporary debates about religious freedom, tolerance, and the role of the state in regulating religious practice.

entities.summary: Enrique de Cardona y Enríquez (1485–1530) was a Spanish Roman Catholic cardinal and bishop. Born in Castell Palau d'Arbeca, Catalonia, Spain, he was appointed Bishop of Barcelona at the age of 21. Enrique de Cardona y Enríquez played a significant role in the Catholic Reformation, serving as a key advisor to Pope Clement VII. He also participated in the councils of Trent and Pisa, shaping the doctrine of the Catholic Church. Enrique de Cardona y Enríquez was a prolific writer and theologian, producing numerous treatises on Catholic doctrine and spiritual practices. His most famous work, 'De vera fide et caritate,' remains a seminal text in Catholic theology. Enrique de Cardona y Enríquez died on February 17, 1530, in Rome, Italy, leaving behind a legacy of spiritual guidance and theological scholarship.
